bug_semantics: The standard HR employee-creation flow at POST /rrhh/employee/save accepted an email address but exposed and validated no password field. EmployeeSaveController nevertheless created the application's normal Authenticatable User record with bcrypt($request->input('password', 'changeme')); because the bundled form could not submit a password, every normally onboarded employee received the predictable password changeme. An unauthenticated remote attacker who knew an onboarded employee's email address could therefore use the ordinary email/password login and obtain that employee account's reachable data and actions.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable HR module was squash-merged to main as 04d1afd73226b1572fd19dc5ee5bbb55b82a1a64 (PR #258), but that aggregate is not the smallest BIC. The PR patch decomposes into 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6 followed by 8369823e08d5ce346527ae6950a588619f821bc6. Atomic member 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6 first added EmployeeSaveController with the changeme fallback, the password-less employee form, and the save route; 8369823e08d5ce346527ae6950a588619f821bc6 only added a missing payroll update route.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6` shows author and committer Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com> and only the subject `feat: New RRHH module with employee management, time tracking, payroll, and company holiday calendar`; there is no Co-authored-by, Generated-with, or other AI attribution trailer, and neither identity is a bot.
evidence: In the validated clone, `git log 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6 --reverse -S'bcrypt($request->input('password', 'changeme'))' -- app/Http/Controllers/Rrhh/Employee/EmployeeSaveController.php` resolves the first writer to 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6, and `git log -L 27,30:app/Http/Controllers/Rrhh/Employee/EmployeeSaveController.php 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6` shows that exact assignment added from /dev/null. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 9e4f84ece7e13c2c327540804dcaf841c6ac23fa -- app/Http/Controllers/Rrhh/Employee/EmployeeSaveController.php resources/views/rrhh/employee/_form.blade.php routes/module/rrhh.php` returns no paths, while the parent-to-BIC diff reports all three as added, directly proving parent absence. The first-party PR #258 patch names members 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6 and 8369823e08d5ce346527ae6950a588619f821bc6; `git rev-parse 8369823e08d5ce346527ae6950a588619f821bc6^{tree} 04d1afd73226b1572fd19dc5ee5bbb55b82a1a64^{tree}` returns the same tree a74da6513163046124c133789294353d268087bd for the final member and squash merge. At the BIC, EmployeeSaveController extends MainController (whose middleware includes auth and locked), POST /rrhh/employee/save invokes save(), the employee form has email but no password input, User extends Authenticatable with email and password fillable, and the guest LoginController uses Laravel's AuthenticatesUsers with the normal email/password form. `version.php` is 5.9.2 in the parent and 5.10.0 in the BIC. The main-history squash 04d1afd73226b1572fd19dc5ee5bbb55b82a1a64 is contained by tag v5.14.0, whose version.php says 5.14.0, proving a tagged vulnerable release; the fix parent e0f3111185035179a0453a717cf67bf9a0eba572 says 5.14.3. The first-party advisory states affected before 5.15.9. PR #263 member c58853a4e3d4cdb554955363a8d0ea8946c869e8 directly removes the changeme assignment and uses a random 16-character password; the squash fix 5cc01ed958db4ad0a026a8daa1c6a8bb98a43e66 contains the final stronger flow (random 32-character password, must-change flag, reset link) and changes version.php to 5.15.9. `git tag --contains 5cc01ed958db4ad0a026a8daa1c6a8bb98a43e66` is empty, so no repository tag contains the fix; `git tag --contains 04d1afd73226b1572fd19dc5ee5bbb55b82a1a64` returns v5.14.0. Existing accounts created with changeme remain weak until their passwords are reset, as the first-party solution notes.
reasoning: The vulnerability requires the combination written atomically by PR member 33a30a5d0de8714198b063742405aa82ae9abda6: a predictable literal fallback, a standard form unable to override it, creation of the same User model accepted by the public login, and a reachable employee save route for normal onboarding. Its immediate parent lacks the HR controller, form, and route, so this is the smallest true BIC rather than the later squash aggregate. The direct fix member c58853a4e3d4cdb554955363a8d0ea8946c869e8 first eliminates the shared credential; the published main-history fix 5cc01ed958db4ad0a026a8daa1c6a8bb98a43e66 lands the final reset-link design at 5.15.9. AI judgment is restricted to the BIC object: it has a human author/committer and no AI attribution marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI regardless of bot-authored PR commentary or later commits.
